title: Pseudorandomness and Diffraction
summary: Pseudorandom structures are structures that behave like random ones, without necessarily being random themselves. It is a prominent, and evidently very difficult, conjecture that $$ V(n) = λ\cos \Big( 2 π\Big( x_1 + n x_2 + \frac{n(n-1)}{2} α\Big) \Big) $$ is pseudorandom from a Schrödinger operator perspective in that the Schrödinger operator in $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})$ with potential $V$ displays Anderson localization, that is, pure point spectrum with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions for almost all parameter values --- the same spectral features as those produced by random potentials.
